note.question: How do batching and optimal multistage bipartite allocations interact?
note.overview: In several applications of real-time matching of demand to supply in online marketplaces, the platform allows for some latency to batch the demand and improve the efficiency of the resulting matching. Motivated by these applications, we study the optimal trade-off between batching and inefficiency in the context of designing robust online allocations. As our base model, we consider K-stage variants of the classic vertex-weighted bipartite b-matching in the adversarial setting, where online vertices arrive stagewise and in K batches—in contrast to online arrival.

source.quote: In several applications of real-time matching of demand to supply in online marketplaces, the platform allows for some latency to batch the demand and improve the efficiency of the resulting matching.

Also, although we allow for free disposal in the extension model, as allocations of an advertiser’s capacity can value differently (i.e., be at a different price level) for different users and config­ urations, for the special case of vertex-weighted match­ ing, there is no point in free disposal by any multistage algorithm, as all allocations of an offline node’s capac­ ity value the same.

As digital consumption behaviors change and new technologies provide new ways for users to interact with social media platforms and publishers, tradi­ tional forms of real-time internet ad allocations also evolve.

In this context, when a user starts watching a new video session (e.g., on You­ Tube), an advertising opportunity to display video ads, and hence allocate user impressions to advertisers and charge them based on per-impression rates, is cre­ ated.

Besides video advertising, there are also other re­ source allocation applications with latency allowance, for example, matching delivery requests to dispatching centers in Amazon or matching user jobs to computing servers in the Azure cloud computing platform.

To systematically extend the above balanced match­ ing idea under the online setting to the multistage setting—where the algorithm can basically match multi­ ple vertices of the arriving batch to the offline side—we propose using specific stage-dependent convex programs and output their optimal solution in each stage as the fractional matching of that stage.
Baseline Model: Multistage Vertex- Weighted Matching We study vertex-weighted matching as our baseline bipar­ tite allocation model for matching arriving demand requests to available supply.
